title: GPT-6.2 Astra API Pricing: What It Costs in 2026
summary: GPT 6.2 Astra API pricing has no confirmed per-token rate available. You'll need to contact the provider directly to get actual pricing.
body_markdown:
## Controlling Astra spend with Activepieces workflows


Only when Astra calls already run inside automated workflows does Activepieces earn its place.


There it can route easy tasks to cheaper models, reuse answers and bound retries, and on Plus ($20 a month, pricing page checked 2026-10-23) with your own AI keys every AI step is 1 credit while the token cost stays on your OpenAI bill, meaning you'll pay both credits and token costs.


It does not touch the listed rate.


### Which Astra workflow steps cost money


Activepieces is useful here because the steps that spend money are ordinary steps you can see and edit, in an MIT-licensed core with 750 integrations.


In the example flow below, a weekly schedule pulls rows from a spreadsheet.


It then loops over them, calls an HTTP endpoint, passes results through two AI steps, writes a row back, and uses a router to decide whether to send an email, so processing time per record scales with the sum of these sequential latencies.


Each of those steps maps to a cost lever.


Splitting that flow into more, smaller steps adds cost, since every AI step is 1 credit.


Activepieces' pricing page, checked 2026-10-23, lists the Free plan at 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows, and counts a run as 1 credit however many steps it has, whereas Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module.


AI steps add credits on top and Astra's tokens still bill at OpenAI's rates, so the workflow line stays flat while the listed rate stays where it was.


### Cutting Astra costs with routing and caching


Start with the router, which is the routing lever. Send a classification or extraction row to GPT-6 Luna, the model OpenAI positions for high-volume work, and let only the rows that fail a condition fall through to Astra.


Your cost per finished task then becomes a blend, not the flagship rate.


For caching, the lever is the write-back step. Insert each answer into a sheet, and look up the sheet before the AI step runs, so a repeated prompt costs one lookup instead of one generation.


That is a pattern you build yourself, not a switch you flip.


### Capping Astra retries and workflow limits


The loop is the retry lever. Because the loop wraps the AI call, you decide how many passes a failing row gets, and the final email step becomes your alert when the cap is hit.


What follows is the limit. If you call the API directly, a few times a day, from a script or a chat window, this machinery costs more in setup and upkeep than it saves.


Past the Free allowance, Plus is $20 a month for 10,000 credits and $0.007 a credit beyond that (pricing page, checked 2026-10-23), so count your runs before assuming the platform costs nothing at your volume.
